topics.title: dot product
topics.essence: How much of one vector lies along another: |a||b|cos θ. Zero when they are perpendicular.
topics.check: a·b is negative. Without computing anything, what does the picture look like?

topics.title: projection
topics.essence: The shadow one vector casts on another. Any b splits into a part along a and a part across it.
topics.check: You double the length of a. What happens to the shadow of b on a, and what happens to a·b?

topics.title: cross product
topics.essence: How much of one vector lies across another: |a||b|sin θ, the signed area the two span. Zero when they are parallel.
topics.check: Swap a and b. What changes in the picture, and why does the sign flip?

topics.title: determinant
topics.essence: The factor by which a matrix scales area. Zero means it flattens the plane onto a line.
topics.check: A matrix has determinant −2. What does it do to the area of a shape, and what does the minus sign do to it?

topics.title: linear systems
topics.essence: Ax = b asks which mix of the columns of A lands on b.
topics.check: The two columns of A point along the same line and b is off that line. How many solutions does Ax = b have, and why?

topics.title: eigenvectors
topics.essence: The directions a matrix only stretches and never turns.
topics.check: A matrix turns every vector by 90°. Can it have a real eigenvector? What would that vector have to do?

links.why: Divide a·b by |a| and what is left is the length of the shadow of b on a.
The part of b that projection leaves behind, the part across a, is exactly what the cross product measures.
In two dimensions a × b is det[a b]: the signed area of the parallelogram on a and b.
A non-zero determinant means the columns still span the space, so Ax = b has exactly one answer.
Eigenvalues are the λ that make det(A − λI) vanish.
